reply: A stop order is an instruction to buy or sell a security once its price reaches a specified level, called the stop price. For a sell stop, the order becomes a market sell when the price falls to the stop price, helping limit losses or protect gains. For a buy stop, the order becomes a market buy when the price rises to the stop price, allowing you to enter a position as a trend continues. In this simulated workstation, stop orders aren’t supported – only market orders at the current price are allowed.
